top.title: 2027: Court sacks ADC governorship candidate in Adamawa
top.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday ordered the removal of Tukur Ribadu as the 2027 Adamawa governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). Justice Obiora Egwuatu, in a judgment, held that Mr Omar Suleiman, who won the majority of the valid votes cast in the primary election of the party, was unlawfully substituted by Ribadu. Justice Egwuatu ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately restore Suleiman as the rightful candidate of the party. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Suleiman, a cousin of former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Babachir Lawal, was said to have initially emerged as the ADC’s candidate in the Adamawa primary. However, he was later replaced by Ribadu. Dissatisfied, Suleiman filed a suit marked FHC/ABJ/C’S/1751/2026 before Justice Egwuatu to challenge his unlawful substitution. He prayed the court to order the ADC to forward his name to the electoral umpire as a valid candidate of the party. He also prayed the court to compel INEC to publish his name as the candidate of the party. Delivering the judgment, Justice Egwuatu held that Suleiman could only be replaced as a candidate if he had formally and voluntarily withdrawn from the race or died. He ruled that since Suleiman had neither withdrawn nor died, his replacement was illegal, null and void. The judge consequently ordered INEC to immediately restore his name as the ADC governorship candidate for Adamawa State in the forthcoming governorship poll. top.description: Over 45 pipeline repairs completed, says commissioner By Hadiza Yusuf KANO — The Kano State Government has warned residents against vandalism, illegal connections and other activities capable of damaging public water infrastructure and disrupting the supply of drinking water across the state. The Commissioner for Water Resources, Dr Dahiru Muhammad Hashim, gave the warning at a press conference in Kano on Friday while briefing journalists on the progress of ongoing rehabilitation of water facilities and restoration of supply to communities. Hashim said the ministry had identified cases of unauthorised connections to water pipelines, vandalism, indiscriminate drilling around major water lines and improper handling of distribution valves. He added that some water pipes had also been damaged by construction activities, refuse burning and other activities around drainage channels. “We appeal to the general public to cooperate with the Ministry in protecting water infrastructure. Our assessment has identified cases of unauthorised tapping of pipelines, vandalism and damage to pipes crossing drainage channels,” he said. The commissioner urged residents, contractors and those executing construction, road and drainage projects to consult relevant authorities before embarking on activities that could affect water pipelines. He also called on residents to promptly report burst pipes, leakages, suspected vandalism and illegal connections to the appropriate authorities. According to him, the restoration of water supply has exposed weaknesses in some old pipelines, many of which had remained without regular water flow for several years. He explained that the return of water pressure to the distribution network had resulted in leakages and pipe bursts in some locations, necessitating urgent repairs and replacement of damaged infrastructure. Hashim disclosed that the ministry had completed more than 45 repair and replacement interventions across different parts of the metropolis. The affected areas include Goron Dutse, Jakara, Kofar Ruwa, Kurmi, Dukawa, Kofar Wambai, Fagge, Club Road, Tudun Wada, Gidan Zakka, Gabari, Koki, Mandawari and Sharada. He said the interventions involved replacing damaged asbestos-cement pipes, fixing leaking PVC pipelines, installing valves and repairing faulty connections. The commissioner further disclosed that water had been pumped from Challawa Water Works to the Goron Dutse reservoirs, which have a reported capacity of 42.5 million litres, before being released into the distribution network. He listed communities that had received water to include Goron Dutse, Gwammaja, Jakara, Kofar Mazugal, Muskwani, Kofar Wambai, Mandawari, Fagge, Tudun Wada, Gama, Kofar Ruwa and Alfindiki, among others. top.title: With Dylan Harper out, Spurs turn to familiar face to fill the void
top.description: San Antonio Spurs forward Julian Champagnie (30) hugs teammate Victor Wembanyama (1) as they celebrate a 124-112 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers in an NBA basketball game, Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, in San Antonio. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Whether coming off the bench or starting, at home or on the road, a pre-game nap is a must for the Spurs' Julian Champagnie. "If you let me, I'll sleep for four hours," he said. Champagnie typically wakes up from his midday snooze rested and ready to go. That was certainly the case Thursday night when he scored 10 of his 20 points in the fourth quarter on 4-of-6 shooting, a flurry that helped the Spurs capture a 124-112 win over the Los Angeles Clippers before a sellout crowd of 18,532 at the Frost Bank Center. The grind-it-out victory - the Clippers trailed by just two points midway through the fourth after overcoming a 14-point second-quarter deficit - represented a nice bounce back for the Spurs following a loss to Detroit two days earlier that snapped their 12-game winning streak. It also highlighted Champagnie's value as a versatile good soldier. He moved into the starting lineup after the Spurs learned earlier in the day they would be without the dynamic Dylan Harper for two to three weeks following the 20-year-old's diagnosis of a left hip external rotator strain. "He's been doing it for a while for this team," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said, referring to Champagnie's skill at filling whatever role is asked of him. Harper sustained the injury when he slipped on the court late in Tuesday's 105-93 loss to the Pistons while attempting to catch a pass from Stephon Castle. It was a scary moment for the Spurs as they watched their second-leading scorer clutch at his groin as he lay on the court in visible pain. But they let out a big sigh of relief after learning Harper did not suffer a serious injury and could be back on the court as soon as early December. "The visuals and optics of falls, potential injuries, whatever you want to call it, can be impressionable, and that one did not look great," Johnson said. "And so there's a lot of WebMD (searching), and you try to not let your mind run the wrong way. You hope for the best, but you really don't know. And it's part of things we can't control. "So just very lucky, fortunate, and mostly just happy for Dylan. Obviously, there'll be some (recovery) time, but very best-case scenario for a lot of the things that could have been." top.title: Tinubu Must Stay group set to unveil presidential library, reform observatory
top.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation TMS, popularly known as Tinubu Must Stay, has announced plans to establish a National Reform Documentation and Impact Observatory, a public digital policy archive and a possible future presidential library for President Bola Tinubu. Chairman of the Board of Trustees and National Coordinator of the group, Malam Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, disclosed this on Friday during the commissioning of its National Secretariat in Abuja. He said the records would start with Tinubu’s years as Governor of Lagos State between 1999 and 2007, then cover policy developments under successive administrations, his national political career and his presidency from 2023. According to him, the archive would span public revenue administration, infrastructure, investment, education, economic management, digital transformation and institutional development. Students, researchers, historians, policymakers and ordinary citizens would be given access to original documents, implementation records, economic data and independent assessments. Inuwa said the library, the observatory and the archive remained long-term aspirations that would need feasibility studies, sustainable funding, proper governance and professional archival standards. “History serves future generations when it preserves evidence, not merely admiration,” he said. He added that the documentation must make room for achievements, implementation difficulties, independent criticism and lessons learned. The announcement came with a membership claim. Inuwa said the group, formally launched on October 1, 2026, had recorded 61,093 validated members within seven weeks across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). He said the group had representation in 730 of the country’s 774 local government areas, about 94 per cent geographical coverage. Its digital database also captures 4,750 wards and 22,584 polling units. Inuwa said 65 per cent of members, roughly 40,000 people, were aged between 18 and 34, while the membership was 65 per cent men and 35 per cent women. “The most remarkable feature of our membership is its youthful composition. top.title: PGA Tour pros embrace clearer pathway under 2028 competitive overhaul
top.description: ST. SIMONS ISLAND, Ga. – The PGA Tour's sweeping competitive overhaul , approved Monday by the Tour's board, is being welcomed by players who believe the new structure will create a simpler, more merit-based path to golf's highest level when it launches in 2028. The changes, developed by the Tour's Future Competition Committee, introduce a revamped promotion system centered on a new Challenger Series and expanded opportunities for players to advance based strictly on performance. PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp outlined the new structure, but committee member Maverick McNealy perhaps best captured the motivation behind the overhaul. He described the previous system as a patchwork of rules that had evolved over time and said the committee started with a simple objective: build a format that is fair, competitive and easy to understand. "It was a really kind of tangled, convoluted system that had evolved over time, little tweaks here and there," McNealy said. At the center of the changes is a more clearly defined pathway to the PGA Tour's highest level. McNealy believes the new structure addresses a longstanding problem for players with limited status, who often spend much of a season waiting to learn when and where they will compete. Under the current system, players without full status can find themselves chasing opportunities, entering events that may not fit their schedules and competing against players with access to the Tour's biggest tournaments. “Those guys don't know when they're going to play,” McNealy said. “There's a lot of guys that get caught in that churn that don't have the opportunity to separate themselves against their peers. I think that's going to be a really compelling part of the Challenger Series is how clear-cut the competition is.” The new model also expands opportunities for Korn Ferry Tour members, with 10 players earning promotion to the Championship Series. McNealy expects that change to make the 2028 Korn Ferry Tour season one of the most competitive in the circuit's history. “I think we're going to have the most compelling season on the Korn Ferry Tour in history because 10 players from the Korn Ferry Tour are going to the Championship Series, which is a huge opportunity for those guys,” he said. He believes the system will be most effective because advancement is based strictly on performance. “Frankly, if you start deciding where people go, people get upset, but if you tell everyone to play for it, this is the number you've got to get to, whoever plays the best wins,” McNealy said. “So the more meritocratic system we can have, the more excited everyone's going to be about it.” Not everyone is ready to declare the changes a success, but early reaction from players was generally positive. (Jess Koehler/For the Times Union) Alicia Collier is the Section 2 girls' volleyball coordinator. In that capacity, she spends a weekend in November every year in Glens Falls serving as the state tournament director at Harding Mazzotti Arena. Also the head coach for South Glens Falls, Collier has her players help out during the state tournament each year, too. This weekend, Collier and her Bulldogs are heading to Harding Mazzotti Arena in a different capacity - one of four teams competing in the Class A bracket. Earlier this month, South Glens Falls captured its first sectional title since winning the 2001 Class B title with a 3-1 decision over Foothills Council rival Glens Falls. top.title: There's an impostor hiding in the Hyades star cluster. Can you spot it?
top.description: null For years I looked at Taurus and saw something perfectly sensible. There was the Hyades, the big V-shaped cluster that forms the bull's face, with Aldebaran, noticeably brighter and more orange than the other stars, the dominant star. Every diagram reinforced the arrangement — Aldebaran was the eye of Taurus, the Hyades made the face, and in my head they became one object. Then I discovered that Aldebaran has nothing to do with the Hyades. I remember going outside afterward and looking again, half expecting the deception to become obvious now that I knew. It didn't. Aldebaran still looked completely at home among the other stars . The difference is hidden in the one dimension our eyes judge poorly when we look into space — depth. Aldebaran is about 65 light-years away, while the Hyades are roughly 150 light-years distant. The orange eye of Taurus is a foreground star that happens to lie almost exactly along our line of sight toward the Hyades. This fact exposes one of the most convincing tricks in stargazing. The night sky looks flat, and our brains are extremely willing to believe it. But it has incredible depth — and when you can see parts of the night sky in 3D, that's when you begin to appreciate that you're not looking at a flat map. Instead, you begin to see our cosmic neighborhood as it really is. By appreciating depth, you learn its geography. What's happening and when to look Aldebaran, the brightest star in the constellation of Taurus. (Image credit: Christophe Lehenaff via Getty Images) Taurus is now easy to find from the Northern Hemisphere during the evening. Once it's dark, look east for a small, tight knot of stars — the Pleiades open cluster (M45) — and then look nearby for a much larger V-shaped arrangement. That V is the Hyades, with unmistakably orange Aldebaran apparently sitting on one arm. Aldebaran's name is derived from the Arabic Al Dabarān, meaning "the follower," because it appears to trail the Pleiades across the night sky. The Hyades is a real physical group of stars — an open cluster — that formed together and moves through our galaxy together. About 153 light-years away, the Hyades is the nearest open star cluster to Earth. The name means "the rainmakers" because their rising and setting times in the ancient Greek sky coincided with wet weather. The stars in the Hyades are of a similar age — and mostly sun-like stars, or similar — so astronomers can tell that they all formed together in the same nebula . Orange-red star Aldebaran — the 14th-brightest star in the night sky — is the interloper, sitting less than half as far away from the sun . If you could somehow view the neighborhood from another part of the Milky Way , the familiar arrangement would fall apart. top.title: Conte: ‘I would love to join an organised club, rather than always adding value’
top.description: Conte: ‘I would love to join an organised club, rather than always adding value’ Antonio Conte insists he would love ‘before ending my career to take over a club that is already organised’ after years of ‘building value’ from troubled situations like Juventus, Chelsea, Inter and Napoli. The coach is currently between jobs after walking away from Napoli in two years where he won the Serie A title and the Supercoppa Italiana. There were reports he could come to Manchester United or even return to his old side Juve, but he is in no rush for his next role. Speaking to the Cronache di Spogliatoio podcast , Conte did outline his greatest strength, and why he perhaps eager to cast it aside and do something different next time. Conte on building clubs up GENOA, ITALY – FEBRUARY 7: Antonio Conte, head coach of Napoli, looks on prior to kick-off in the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and SSC Napoli at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on February 7, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images) “There is one thing I’d love to do before ending my career as a coach, which is to take over a club that is already organised,” said Conte. “It would be like stepping into a Formula 1 car in pole position. It never happened in my career, but evidently that is just the way it goes for me. I always arrived at complicated situations and was fortunate, but also deserve credit, for taking a team back to victory. “Often, it involved returning them to their history, a dimension that perhaps they had forgotten.” It all sounds like the scenario at Manchester United, who have not won the Premier League since 2013, following in the footsteps of other clubs he went through. LONDON, ENGLAND – JANUARY 08: John Terry of Chelsea (L) walks off after being sent off and shakes hands with Antonio Conte, Manager of Chelsea (R) during The Emirates FA Cup Third Round match between Chelsea and Peterborough United at Stamford Bridge on January 8, 2017 in London, England. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images) “It happened at Juventus, who got back to winning after seven years, Inter hadn’t won the Scudetto for 10, and Chelsea were coming off a disastrous season when I arrived, finishing in 10 th place, but then won the Premier League with me. “The same was true at Napoli, where they had finished 10 th , then I arrived and took them to victory.” That also means Conte brings with him certain expectations, something he is quick to point out in press conferences from the very start. “It is inevitable that when you arrive with a curriculum like this, you are accompanied by big expectations. People and the media expect you to win. I still remember when I arrived at Napoli, a team that finished 10 th , a beautiful city, their objective was to qualify for the Champions League. “I thought I could just enjoy my work and the city for a while, but the moment I signed, the media completely changed the message. top.title: Nick Saban reveals how view of ‘traditional’ blue-blood jobs has changed in NIL era
top.description: As the college football regular season winds down, the coaching carousel is starting to spin. Some notable jobs are in the spotlight, including Florida State after the firing of Mike Norvell earlier this month. But in the NIL and transfer portal era, the view of traditional blue-blood jobs has changed, according to former Alabama coach Nick Saban . Now, resources are the name of the game when it comes to building rosters – but that’s just one part of the equation. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage “I think the ‘traditional’ really good jobs are no longer the best jobs,” Saban said Friday on The Pat McAfee Show . “And I think the way you look at a job is completely different than the way you would’ve done five years ago, 10 years ago. “Because now, it’s all about what kind of resources do we have to build a squad. Now, on the other side of that is because people can transfer, how many players could you bring with you if you went someplace else to turn a program around quickly?” Saban specifically cited the turnarounds at UCLA and Indiana . Bob Chesney has the Bruins undefeated entering Week 12 while Curt Cignetti took the Hoosiers from the losingest program in college football history to national champions in just two years. Both coaches came from James Madison and had key players re-join them at their new stops. Saban said that, along with having the proper resources, impacts the discussion around some of college football’s top jobs. “I think the dynamic is completely different,” Saban said. “If you don’t think you have the resources to sustain success where you are right now – and resources is about money right now, paying players. That’s what it comes down to. Then, maybe you’re better off taking a job where you do have the resources.” “If you think you have the resources, continuity is something that’s probably a little easier to build on if you do have the resources to continue to be able to grow your squad. Because your squad’s going to change every year.” The approach to roster-building is also important. In the era of player movement, backups could opt to enter the transfer portal and seek starting roles. That’s why coaches have to decide how to build the entire roster. “And then, what’s your philosophy of building your squad?” Nick Saban said. “How many significant players do you get, how many backup players do you lose, how many guys can you bring in for cheap that’ll take the place of those backup players? “So it’s building your squad from top to bottom, your roster. Some guys can do that pretty well. Some guys might struggle with it.”

Justice Egwuatu ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately restore Suleiman as the rightful candidate of the party. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Suleiman, a cousin of former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Babachir Lawal, was said to have initially emerged as the ADC’s candidate in the Adamawa primary. However, he was later replaced by Ribadu. Dissatisfied, Suleiman filed a suit marked FHC/ABJ/C’S/1751/2026 before Justice Egwuatu to challenge his unlawful substitution. He prayed the court to order the ADC to forward his name to the electoral umpire as a valid candidate of the party. He also prayed the court to compel INEC to publish his name as the candidate of the party. Delivering the judgment, Justice Egwuatu held that Suleiman could only be replaced as a candidate if he had formally and voluntarily withdrawn from the race or died. He ruled that since Suleiman had neither withdrawn nor died, his replacement was illegal, null and void. The judge consequently ordered INEC to immediately restore his name as the ADC governorship candidate for Adamawa State in the forthcoming governorship poll. nigeria.description: Over 45 pipeline repairs completed, says commissioner By Hadiza Yusuf KANO — The Kano State Government has warned residents against vandalism, illegal connections and other activities capable of damaging public water infrastructure and disrupting the supply of drinking water across the state. The Commissioner for Water Resources, Dr Dahiru Muhammad Hashim, gave the warning at a press conference in Kano on Friday while briefing journalists on the progress of ongoing rehabilitation of water facilities and restoration of supply to communities. Hashim said the ministry had identified cases of unauthorised connections to water pipelines, vandalism, indiscriminate drilling around major water lines and improper handling of distribution valves. He added that some water pipes had also been damaged by construction activities, refuse burning and other activities around drainage channels. “We appeal to the general public to cooperate with the Ministry in protecting water infrastructure. Our assessment has identified cases of unauthorised tapping of pipelines, vandalism and damage to pipes crossing drainage channels,” he said. The commissioner urged residents, contractors and those executing construction, road and drainage projects to consult relevant authorities before embarking on activities that could affect water pipelines. He also called on residents to promptly report burst pipes, leakages, suspected vandalism and illegal connections to the appropriate authorities. According to him, the restoration of water supply has exposed weaknesses in some old pipelines, many of which had remained without regular water flow for several years. He explained that the return of water pressure to the distribution network had resulted in leakages and pipe bursts in some locations, necessitating urgent repairs and replacement of damaged infrastructure. Hashim disclosed that the ministry had completed more than 45 repair and replacement interventions across different parts of the metropolis. The affected areas include Goron Dutse, Jakara, Kofar Ruwa, Kurmi, Dukawa, Kofar Wambai, Fagge, Club Road, Tudun Wada, Gidan Zakka, Gabari, Koki, Mandawari and Sharada. He said the interventions involved replacing damaged asbestos-cement pipes, fixing leaking PVC pipelines, installing valves and repairing faulty connections. nigeria.title: Nigeria to become world’s third-largest Muslim population by 2035 – Report
nigeria.description: Nigeria is projected to have the world’s third-largest Muslim population by 2035, behind Pakistan and India, as Islam is expected to record significant growth globally over the next decade. The projection is contained in a report by the Pew Research Centre titled Future of World Religions, released on Wednesday. According to the report, Muslims are expected to outnumber Christians globally by 2070 if current demographic trends continue, marking a significant shift in the religious composition of the world. The report projects that the global Muslim population will exceed 3.6 billion by 2070, compared with just under three billion Christians. It attributed the projected growth largely to differences in fertility rates, noting that Muslim women had an average of 3.1 children between 2020 and 2025, compared with 2.5 for Christian women and 1.6 for women belonging to other religious groups. The report explained that a population requires an average of about 2.1 children per woman to maintain its size across generations. Under the projections, Pakistan will have the world’s largest Muslim population by 2035, followed by India, Nigeria and Indonesia, which currently has the largest Muslim population. The findings further indicated that four of the 10 countries with the largest Muslim populations by 2070 would be in Africa, namely Nigeria, Egypt, Ethiopia and Sudan. The Pew Research Centre’s projections cover 201 countries and territories, accounting for 99.98 per cent of the world’s population. It said the estimates were based on the assumption that existing trends in fertility, mortality and religious switching would continue, while acknowledging that developments such as wars, natural disasters and economic changes could alter the projections. The report also projected significant changes in the global Christian population, particularly in the United States, which is expected to lose its Christian-majority status, although Christians would remain the country’s largest religious group. It further predicted that the Democratic Republic of the Congo would overtake the United States as the country with the largest Christian population. For centuries, Christianity has remained the world’s largest religion, but the latest projections point to a gradual shift in the global religious landscape, driven largely by population growth and demographic differences. nigeria.title: Tinubu’s NYSC certificate: Court dismisses Atiku, ADC application
nigeria.description: A Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed an application by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) seeking to amend their suit challenging President Bola Tinubu’s eligibility for the 2027 presidential election over his National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) discharge certificate. In a ruling on Friday, according to TheCable, Justice Inyang Ekwo held that the proposed amendments would introduce new facts and alter the substance of the original case. The judge upheld the arguments by Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) that the applicants were attempting to introduce a fresh allegation of fraud after the defendants had responded to the original suit. Ekwo noted that pre-election cases were sui generis, meaning they belonged to a special category of legal proceedings and were subject to strict timelines. He added that litigants could not institute such actions and subsequently search for evidence to support their claims. The judge also faulted the applicants for failing to challenge claims in the defendants’ counter-affidavits that the proposed amendments were intended to mislead the court. “This is a time-bound suit, and the law makes it mandatory for all exhibits to be filed in court within 14 days of the occurrence of the event being challenged. Anything outside the prescribed 14 days is null and void and of no effect,” the judge held. “I find no merit in this application to bring a fresh exhibit; it is hereby refused for being against the express provision of the law. “I hereby make an order dismissing this application, and it is hereby dismissed,” he ruled. The matter was adjourned until December 2 for hearing. Atiku and the ADC had filed the substantive suit on August 14, seeking an order disqualifying Tinubu and the APC from the 2027 presidential election over an allegation that the NYSC discharge certificate submitted by the President to INEC was forged. They also sought an order compelling the electoral commission to remove Tinubu’s name and the APC from the list of candidates and political parties for the election. Following the defendants’ responses, Atiku and the ADC approached the court on September 10, seeking to amend their originating summons. They said the proposed amendments were intended to correct errors in the description of INEC forms attached to their affidavit, provide clearer copies of exhibits, include particulars of the alleged fraud and incorporate Atiku’s written deposition. However, Tinubu opposed the application, arguing that the proposed changes went beyond correcting errors and would introduce new facts, documents and reliefs. nigeria.title: Many feared dead as overloaded boat capsizes in Bayelsa
nigeria.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa Many passengers are feared dead after a cargo boat conveying more than 300 persons capsized in the riverine area of Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State on Friday. The ill-fated vessel was reportedly travelling from Anyama Ijaw to Ukubie community when the incident occurred between 12 noon and 1pm. Preliminary reports indicated that the boat, which was allegedly overloaded with passengers travelling to attend a burial ceremony, capsized in the waterways between Oweikorogha and Angiama communities. Eyewitness accounts suggested that the tragedy might have been averted, as some passengers reportedly advised the boat operator to stop at Oweikorogha to reduce the number of persons on board. However, the advice was allegedly ignored, and the boat reportedly capsized shortly after leaving the community. Although the actual casualty figure remained unknown as of the time of filing this report, fears were mounting that the death toll could be high, given the number of passengers on board. The Chairman of the State Maritime Workers Union, Mr Ipigansi Igoniba, confirmed the incident to our correspondent but said details of the disaster were still sketchy. “I cannot give the casualty figure right now. We have sent our members to the scene of the accident, and search and rescue efforts for the missing persons are ongoing,” Igoniba said. Rescue operations were ongoing as efforts continued to establish the number of survivors and fatalities. The incident has thrown the affected communities into mourning and renewed concerns over the dangers of overcrowding and unsafe transportation on Bayelsa’s waterways. nigeria.title: The Other Black Gold: Nigeria’s Coffee Sector Wants A Shot
nigeria.description: Richard Ali grew up with the aroma of coffee wafting through his house in central Nigeria as his father, an accountant, worked late into the night, drinking powdered, instant stuff from Maxwell House and Nescafé. It was not until years later, travelling on the other side of the continent, that Ali had a taste of “coffee, coffee — brewed coffee”. “I have to bring this to Nigeria,” he thought, and he started looking into importing beans from Rwanda. Ali later discovered he did not have to: coffee has been growing in Nigeria for more than 100 years. A wave of entrepreneurs in Africa’s most populous country are turning towards the oil-producing nation’s other black gold — an uphill task in a place full of tea and instant coffee, and little sense of homegrown java as a daily staple or part of a wider cultural patrimony. A general view of someone handling coffee beans in a plantation in the Gorongosa mountain range in Gorongosa on May 20, 2022. (Photo by Alfredo Zuniga / AFP) But roasters say they have found a market — and sense of national pride — to tap into, even if Nigeria’s beans are not well-known. “We need to grow more coffee, whether for the domestic market, which is expanding, or the global market, which is now considering Nigerian coffee,” Ali, founder of Tigray Coffee, which launched in 2021, said over a cup of Nigerian brew, light with slightly chocolatey notes. Agricultural Investments In Ethiopia, hundreds of years of cultivation have bound coffee to local culture, while Uganda and Ivory Coast have become modern export powerhouses. Nigeria produced 1,808 tonnes of beans in 2024, according to statistics from the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organisation — a paltry sum compared to Kenya’s 49,500 tonnes that same year. The first seeds hit the ground in Nigeria in the 19th century, after coffee was introduced by British colonists. The crop is notoriously fickle and can only grow in certain parts of the country. But there has also been a dearth of investment in agriculture, critics say, as the government instead became over-reliant on the oil sector for revenues. Experts have long called for a more diversified economy. The government agrees, at least in principle: in May, agriculture minister Abubakar Kyari announced federal investments in coffee production in Ondo State, calling it “a powerful economic crop” that could create jobs and “boost rural livelihoods”. ‘Never Imported Coffee’ At the opening of a new cafe in Lagos last month, Princess Adeyinka Tekenah paired a local brew not with croissants, but puff-puff, a staple street food snack of fried dough. “I have been in the business for 12 years, and I have never imported coffee,” the founder of Happy Coffee said. nigeria.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki Governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru of Ebonyi State has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to judicial independence, stressing the need for an efficient justice system driven by technology and timely dispensation of justice. Nwifuru stated this on Friday at the State High Court, Abakaliki, during the special court session marking the commencement of the 2026/2027 Legal Year in the state. The governor also inaugurated a Magistrate Court complex comprising six court halls and an exhibit hall, constructed under the administration of the Chief Judge of the state, Justice Elvis Ngene. He advocated the adoption of technology-driven processes in the administration of justice, noting that an efficient justice system must be capable of resolving disputes promptly while minimising unnecessary expenditure of resources. According to him, delays in the administration of justice undermine the effective use of resources, while technological innovations provide opportunities to improve judicial processes and enhance access to justice. “A justice system that cannot resolve disputes timely wastes resources. Technology offers us the opportunity to resolve some of these things. Digital filings and digital transcriptions help. “The significance goes beyond governance. It helps to transact with various registries without recourse to location,” he said. Nwifuru explained that deploying digital technology in judicial administration would reduce the challenges associated with physical processes, improve efficiency and enable legal practitioners and litigants to interact with court registries more conveniently. On judicial independence, the governor described the judiciary as a critical institution for sustaining constitutional democracy and checking possible excesses of the executive arm of government. “An independent judiciary checkmates the government as well as its excesses. As a Governor, I recognise that the independence of the judiciary must be respected and allowed to perform its constitutional and professional mandate,” he stated. He said his administration’s People’s Charter of Needs agenda had prioritised reforms in the justice sector, citing the introduction of electronic filing, establishment of a Moot Court, creation of the Office of the Public Defender and adoption of the Sexual Assault Bill as some of the initiatives. The governor said the measures were aimed at strengthening institutional capacity, promoting access to justice and ensuring that the justice system remained responsive to the needs of the people. Earlier, the Chief Judge of Ebonyi State, Justice Elvis Ngene, said the judiciary had recorded progress in several areas of judicial administration in the last year. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal Several researchers have published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a proposed post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the wider community to look for flaws in it. Researcher Mikhail Kudinov announced the first version Thursday in a thread on X, saying the paper reduces SHRINCS’ security to the properties of its underlying hash function. The analysis, dated Nov. 18, estimates classical security of 121.4 to 122.7 bits for SHRINCS, though those figures rest on assumptions that include three unproven conjectures. Kudinov said the work is not finished. The team is still working on a new analysis of a property called SM-DSPR, whose bound has so far been conjectured, and on tightening a reprogramming step and improving a bound against quantum attackers. How SHRINCS works SHRINCS is a hash-based scheme, meaning its security rests on hash functions rather than the elliptic curve math behind today’s Bitcoin signatures. It places two designs under one key: a stateful part built on FXMSS with WOTS+C, and a stateless fallback built on SLH-DSA. Because both use the same hash function, Kudinov said, the proof has to cover both. Signature size is the main cost. Under the draft proposal, stateful SHRINCS signatures run from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while the stateless fallback is 5,777 bytes. Schnorr signatures on Bitcoin today are 64 bytes, and ECDSA signatures typically come in around 71. Signatures take up scarce block space, so larger ones mean fewer transactions per block. The risk of a stateful signature The compact stateful path carries a danger. It relies on one-time keys, and if a wallet accidentally reuses one, an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal the funds. Wallet software therefore has to track the state of every key. The stateless path avoids the problem, but at a much larger size. Jonas Nick, Blockstream’s director of research, told Isabel Foxen Duke, head of the MARA Foundation, on MARA Foundation TV that wallets must automatically fall back to the stateless path whenever a state counter could be compromised. “It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” he said. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.” Nick also warned that heavy use of the larger signatures would weigh on the network. “We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very big signatures,” he said. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. And I think this changes the value proposition of Bitcoin.” Researchers ask for review The authors are clear that the analysis needs scrutiny. business.title: Block Says Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Block Says Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food Most bitcoin payments at Square sellers are small, everyday purchases at coffee shops and restaurants, Block said in a new report that it hopes will inform a debate in Congress over a tax break for small crypto purchases. The report, “The State of Bitcoin Payments,” covers completed bitcoin payments at U.S. Square sellers from Nov. 1, 2025, to Oct. 15, 2026. The median payment was about $13, and the average was about $29. Food and drink businesses took 72% of those payments, Block found. That is a bigger share than the category’s 67.5% slice of regular card payments on Square over the same period. “Most bitcoin payments are small and routine,” the company wrote on X Thursday, calling the report one of the first datasets on how people spend bitcoin in the local economy. Coffee, quick bites and repeat visits Coffee shops and fast food businesses accounted for 62.6% of the bitcoin payments in the food and drink category, with a median payment of $9.10. Grocery stores made up a smaller share but had the highest average payment in the group, at $60.73. Small tickets dominated. About 42% of bitcoin payments on Square were under $10, and 65.1% were under $20. Those sub-$20 payments made up just 19.1% of total payment value, though, with a few larger purchases accounting for much of the dollars spent. Customers also came back. Among Cash App users who paid with bitcoin at least twice at the same merchant, the median was three purchases per customer-merchant pair. About 44% of bitcoin payments from Cash App were repeat payments, and 86% of those came within 30 days. The activity was not limited to Block’s own app. External Lightning wallets such as Strike, Wallet of Satoshi, Phoenix and Coinbase handled 56.6% of Square bitcoin payments and about 66% of payment value, while Cash App wallets made up the rest. Square sellers can choose how much of each sale they keep in bitcoin, and Square converts the rest to dollars automatically. Block said zero-fee processing for bitcoin payments on Square has been extended through Dec. 31, 2027. Local governments are testing similar setups, with Miami-Dade County now taking bitcoin for property taxes and converting it to dollars. Under current U.S. federal rules, paying with bitcoin generally means calculating a capital gain or loss on every purchase, even a $10 coffee, the company said. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. The changes, developed by the Tour's Future Competition Committee, introduce a revamped promotion system centered on a new Challenger Series and expanded opportunities for players to advance based strictly on performance. PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp outlined the new structure, but committee member Maverick McNealy perhaps best captured the motivation behind the overhaul. He described the previous system as a patchwork of rules that had evolved over time and said the committee started with a simple objective: build a format that is fair, competitive and easy to understand. "It was a really kind of tangled, convoluted system that had evolved over time, little tweaks here and there," McNealy said. At the center of the changes is a more clearly defined pathway to the PGA Tour's highest level. McNealy believes the new structure addresses a longstanding problem for players with limited status, who often spend much of a season waiting to learn when and where they will compete. Under the current system, players without full status can find themselves chasing opportunities, entering events that may not fit their schedules and competing against players with access to the Tour's biggest tournaments. “Those guys don't know when they're going to play,” McNealy said. “There's a lot of guys that get caught in that churn that don't have the opportunity to separate themselves against their peers. I think that's going to be a really compelling part of the Challenger Series is how clear-cut the competition is.” The new model also expands opportunities for Korn Ferry Tour members, with 10 players earning promotion to the Championship Series. McNealy expects that change to make the 2028 Korn Ferry Tour season one of the most competitive in the circuit's history. “I think we're going to have the most compelling season on the Korn Ferry Tour in history because 10 players from the Korn Ferry Tour are going to the Championship Series, which is a huge opportunity for those guys,” he said. sports.title: Conte: ‘I would love to join an organised club, rather than always adding value’
sports.description: Conte: ‘I would love to join an organised club, rather than always adding value’ Antonio Conte insists he would love ‘before ending my career to take over a club that is already organised’ after years of ‘building value’ from troubled situations like Juventus, Chelsea, Inter and Napoli. The coach is currently between jobs after walking away from Napoli in two years where he won the Serie A title and the Supercoppa Italiana. There were reports he could come to Manchester United or even return to his old side Juve, but he is in no rush for his next role. Speaking to the Cronache di Spogliatoio podcast , Conte did outline his greatest strength, and why he perhaps eager to cast it aside and do something different next time. Conte on building clubs up GENOA, ITALY – FEBRUARY 7: Antonio Conte, head coach of Napoli, looks on prior to kick-off in the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and SSC Napoli at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on February 7, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images) “There is one thing I’d love to do before ending my career as a coach, which is to take over a club that is already organised,” said Conte. “It would be like stepping into a Formula 1 car in pole position. It never happened in my career, but evidently that is just the way it goes for me. I always arrived at complicated situations and was fortunate, but also deserve credit, for taking a team back to victory. “Often, it involved returning them to their history, a dimension that perhaps they had forgotten.” It all sounds like the scenario at Manchester United, who have not won the Premier League since 2013, following in the footsteps of other clubs he went through. sports.title: Nick Saban reveals how view of ‘traditional’ blue-blood jobs has changed in NIL era
sports.description: As the college football regular season winds down, the coaching carousel is starting to spin. Some notable jobs are in the spotlight, including Florida State after the firing of Mike Norvell earlier this month. But in the NIL and transfer portal era, the view of traditional blue-blood jobs has changed, according to former Alabama coach Nick Saban . Now, resources are the name of the game when it comes to building rosters – but that’s just one part of the equation. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage “I think the ‘traditional’ really good jobs are no longer the best jobs,” Saban said Friday on The Pat McAfee Show . “And I think the way you look at a job is completely different than the way you would’ve done five years ago, 10 years ago. “Because now, it’s all about what kind of resources do we have to build a squad. Now, on the other side of that is because people can transfer, how many players could you bring with you if you went someplace else to turn a program around quickly?” Saban specifically cited the turnarounds at UCLA and Indiana . Bob Chesney has the Bruins undefeated entering Week 12 while Curt Cignetti took the Hoosiers from the losingest program in college football history to national champions in just two years. Both coaches came from James Madison and had key players re-join them at their new stops. Saban said that, along with having the proper resources, impacts the discussion around some of college football’s top jobs. “I think the dynamic is completely different,” Saban said. “If you don’t think you have the resources to sustain success where you are right now – and resources is about money right now, paying players. That’s what it comes down to. Then, maybe you’re better off taking a job where you do have the resources.” “If you think you have the resources, continuity is something that’s probably a little easier to build on if you do have the resources to continue to be able to grow your squad. Because your squad’s going to change every year.” The approach to roster-building is also important. In the era of player movement, backups could opt to enter the transfer portal and seek starting roles. That’s why coaches have to decide how to build the entire roster. “And then, what’s your philosophy of building your squad?” Nick Saban said. “How many significant players do you get, how many backup players do you lose, how many guys can you bring in for cheap that’ll take the place of those backup players? “So it’s building your squad from top to bottom, your roster. Some guys can do that pretty well. Some guys might struggle with it.”

sports.title: For Lions, beating Buccaneers starts with stopping Bucky Irving
sports.description: ALLEN PARK — Entering Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers find themselves in the unique position of having the NFL's No. 1 rushing offense and No. 32 passing offense. In other words, their play style is a linebackers' dream. "This is one of those buckle-your-you-know-what-up games, and let's do it," said defensive coordinator and former NFL linebacker Kelvin Sheppard. "And (it's) mano a mano, they don't hide it, and we don't hide the way we play. So it's a beautiful thing. It's a beautiful challenge, and we're looking forward to it.” While the Lions have the edge in the passing game on Sunday, the run game — which both teams want to ride to victory — is a true strength-on-strength matchup from every angle. More: Why Isaac TeSlaa is ‘inspiration’ to Lions’ selfless receiver room The Buccaneers, averaging a league-best 163.9 yards per game on the ground, will face one of their biggest tests yet, as Detroit ranks fifth in run defense and allows just 90.4 rushing yards per game. Over their last five games, the Lions haven't allowed more than 81 yards on the ground. Opponents are averaging 3.4 yards per carry and 67 yards per game in that span. "This is a linebacker's dream game," linebacker Derrick Barnes said. "Obviously, we take pride in being able to stop the run, being a sound defense when it comes to the run ... it's a part of our identity, stopping the run. That's something that we said at the beginning (of the season). Like, if we do anything, it's going to be able to stop the run." More: Lions' Derrick Barnes eager to face 'best friend' Alex Anzalone and Bucs Leading Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving ranks fifth in rushing yards (825) with seven touchdowns, with Kenneth Gainwell adding 305. sports.title: Formula 1 set for V8 turbo return in 2030
sports.description: Motorsport photo Formula 1 has moved closer to a return to V8 engines from the 2030 season as the FIA announced that a unanimous agreement has been reached between the governing body, F1 management and the power unit manufacturers. F1 has long worked towards cheaper and simpler engines for the next regulation cycle, which starts in 2031, having recognised the current formula is too complex and physically heavy, and a relic of a different direction in the road car industry. The FIA could have set the series’ future power-unit regulations for 2031, when the current cycle ends, but there has been broad alignment within the sport to bring that timeline forward by one year, driven by both president Mohammed Ben Sulayem and F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali. So following recent gatherings by the F1 Commission and power unit advisory committee, where key aspects like the formula, timelines and costs were discussed, there had been broad support to bring forward the next generation of engine regulations by one year and curtail the current formula. The consensus is for F1 to move to a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 engine with a smaller electric component of 200kW, half of which will be ringfenced for overtake-mode use. The 2.1-litre capacity is derived from the current 1.6-litre V6 formula as a starting point, with two additional cylinders intended to reduce development costs. After an aborted announcement on Tuesday, the FIA has now officially confirmed there is unanimous support among its stakeholders about bringing that move forward to 2030. "The FIA presented F1 Power Unit regulations for introduction from 2030 with a 2.1 litre turbocharged V8 as the power unit of choice carrying over some geometrical specifics," the governing body said on Friday. "The overriding objective is to deliver a power unit which is a lot less complex, lighter and cheaper than the current power units. It will feature limited hybridisation, relevant and sustainable technology with the aim of enhancing attack-oriented racing and a sound which resonates with fans. "Additionally, the plan is to marry the V8 power unit to a chassis which will also be lighter, more agile and placing greater emphasis on driver skill and close racing. " F1 and FIA F1 and FIA Ben Sulayem added: "This agreement marks a significant milestone in shaping the future of Formula 1. “From the outset I have been clear in my ambition to deliver a sport that is more competitive and more exciting for our fans, while remaining at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. "The return of V8 engines represents an opportunity to reconnect with the DNA of this championship, bringing back the sound, emotion and pure racing that is loved worldwide. “Our vision is clear, lighter, simpler and more affordable cars that put driver skill at the heart of the competition." technology.title: Nvidia’s journey to forge the one CPU SKU to rule them all
technology.description: Each generation of Intel Xeons or AMD Epycs brings dozens of new SKUs: high-core count parts tuned for throughput, high-frequency ones optimized for latency, low-power chips designed for the edge, and everything in between. But if you ask Ian Finder, who heads development of Nvidia’s datacenter CPUs, for the vast majority of use cases, all those SKUs are overkill. “There was sort of an overskewing, for many years on the other vendors side of things,” he told El Reg on the sidelines of Supercomputing 2026 this week. Nvidia is a relative newcomer to the datacenter CPU space. The company’s first part, called Grace, launched in 2023, but didn’t see widespread deployment outside AI headnodes, high-end NICs, and a handful of standalone CPU deployments by hyperscalers like Meta. We explored the chip in greater detail earlier this year, but the GPU slinger’s latest CPU, Vera, is a different beast. In addition to showing up as part of Nvidia’s Vera-Rubin superchips, the CPU will also be offered in standalone CPU racks, storage, and context memory systems. Just this week, Nvidia announced a new rack with 192 Vera CPUs aimed at high-performance computing (HPC) workloads, which don’t translate well to GPUs. And at least on paper, a single SKU with 88 cores clocking to 3.3 GHz powers all of them. Historically, CPUs with different combinations of cores, clocks, I/O, and power have been used in these roles. According to Finder, most datacenter CPUs haven’t been loaded that heavily, and as a result unloaded latency has been the optimization point. As a consequence, CPUs that rely on high core counts to boost throughput often suffer from elevated loaded latencies. On the flip side, chipmakers can optimize for loaded latency, but this usually comes at the expense of throughput. We see this pretty clearly across AMD’s last few generations of Epycs, where it designed both space-efficient Zen-C cores that prioritize throughput and fatter frequency-optimized versions that prioritize latency. “As more cores are up and running, your latency to memory gets higher because you have to deal with congestion on the connectivity buses,” More than Moore analyst Ian Cutress tells The Reg . “What Nvidia is saying is right. Sometimes, you do have to pick between core count and core latency.” A balanced architecture With Vera, Nvidia sought to thread that needle to design a balanced architecture that maintains low latencies and high throughput even when all 88 cores are loaded. This does mean making some compromises – in particular, the CPU's vector unit isn’t the beefiest. technology.description: Suspected Chinese spies deployed AI agents which worked autonomously to find a zero-day in an open source application and then abuse the flaw to break into university networks, gaining full control of a server, according to Amazon CISO CJ Moses. The China-linked attacker used Cairn, an open source, penetration-testing framework that has become increasingly popular with cybercriminals who use the AI tool to carry out multi-stage intrusions with no human assistance . technology.title: AI boom threatens circuit board crunch to rival pandemic-era chip shortage
technology.description: The electronics industry faces a printed circuit board (PCB) shortage that could rival the pandemic-era chip crunch – with AI once again accused of hogging supplies. The Global Electronics Association says demand is arriving "at a scale the supply chain was not built for," straining everything from glass fabric and resin to finished boards. Its report, " The PCB Squeeze: A Wake-Up Call for Global Electronics ," says AI servers need increasingly complex boards. While a typical PC board has about 12 layers of tracks, AI server boards can have 40 to 60 layers or more, and each additional layer requires more resin, copper foil, and laminate. The supply of materials is set to be constrained through at least the first half of 2027, the report says, with meaningful relief unlikely before mid-2028. Programs to deliver PCBs for automotive, industrial, medical and even the defense industries are being crowded out as AI soaks up scarce capacity, it claims. The association's North American figures show orders growing much faster than deliveries. PCB bookings rose 56.1 percent in the first nine months of 2026 compared with the same period last year, while PCB shipments increased 13.3 percent. Fabrication capacity is expanding, aimed at meeting the increased demand from the AI infrastructure sector, especially in Asia, where more than 90 percent of the world's boards are made. The report says that $10 billion has gone toward new PCB plants in Southeast Asia, and at least as much has been invested in China over the past three years, but the raw materials are themselves constrained. It warns of lengthening lead times for those raw materials. Standard FR-4 laminate now takes six to eight weeks to ship, up from two to three weeks a year ago, while advanced low-loss laminates now take 14 to 18 weeks for delivery, for example. Tightening supplies usually lead to price increases, and the report says that suppliers raised laminate costs by 30 percent in September, and that the price tag of some types of E-glass cloth for circuit boards has risen by 300 percent. The report also puts copper prices up 37 percent over the past year. Concerns have been raised about copper supplies before, as The Register has reported multiple times. The association compares the risk with the 2021 chip shortage , when disrupted supplies left manufacturers unable to secure even relatively mundane components. New capacity is coming, but it is late and comes in dribs and drabs, according to the report, while AI demand just keeps on absorbing it as soon as it arrives. The association's advice is for buyers to plan early, and to share realistic forecasts with suppliers rather than double-booking. Board makers should qualify alternative suppliers of materials such as laminate and copper foil before shortages bite, but it warns against stockpiling beyond real need, which adds to forward-buying pressure. technology.title: Microsoft's last non-security preview of 2026 packs a punch
technology.description: Microsoft has delivered its final scheduled non-security preview update of 2026 for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2, with an updated Windows Search experience and a brighter Windows Hello for users who prefer darker rooms. The optional KB5132057 update arrived on November 19, after this month's Patch Tuesday. Microsoft is skipping December's non-security preview because of reduced holiday operations, though that doesn't cancel the monthly security release. This last preview is quite a doozy. The big-ticket item is the "new Windows Search Experience." We saw a preview of this last month, and Microsoft has gone well beyond the "just make it work" request of many Windows users. Results appear faster with less clutter, the tool uses memory better, and files can be previewed directly in Windows Search. We're less convinced by inline actions, which let users perform common tasks directly through Windows Search without opening Settings. In our testing, "turn on dark mode" worked, but "switch on dark mode" did not, thus highlighting the limitations of the tool. In addition, we remain unconvinced that Windows Search is the place to run actions. That said, anything that makes Windows Search less of a punchline for unkind jokes about performance and accuracy is welcome, as are other features, including an optional screen-brightening feature for Windows Hello facial recognition in dim rooms, and the PowerToys-esque Run dialog, which users can enable in Settings. While some of the new features won't be enabled immediately, Microsoft has included fixes that will be available right away. One addresses an issue where Windows Fax and Scan could fail to connect to a fax server. Handy for those occasions when email falls over into a heap . There are also fixes for Windows IoT Enterprise LTSC activation failures and the misleading "Something went wrong" message shown on Android devices during cross-device passkey authentication. At the time of writing, Microsoft still lists the problem as something for which "we are working on a resolution to be released in a future Windows update." Sadly, not everything has been pushed off the naughty step. SQL Server queries using OLE DB providers can still leave connections to external databases open after they've finished. Microsoft is working on that one and "will provide an update in an upcoming release." ®

technology.title: Microsoft suggests Registry hack to work around hotpatch woes
technology.description: Some Windows 11 applications might fail to install or launch after Microsoft's November hotpatch, but not to worry: there's a Registry tweak to work around it. Microsoft has confirmed it isn't administrators' imaginations. The November hotpatch is causing application errors, including in little-used and obscure apps such as Outlook. Affected applications may fail during installation, launch, or use, displaying errors such as " ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED (0xC0000099) ." Microsoft's investigation points to applications that load the 32-bit Windows Installer DLL, msi.dll. The problem is more common with 32-bit software, but can also affect 64-bit applications "under certain circumstances." The workaround involves fiddling with the Registry on affected devices, so is not for the faint of heart and a backup is a good idea before diving in. Microsoft says the key " HotPatchTableSize " in the folder " HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management " needs to be set to " 2000 " followed by a restart. Just the thing to round out the week for administrators. The issue affects the November hotpatch, not the standard monthly cumulative security update. "Devices which installed the November 2026 Windows monthly security update are not expected to be affected by this issue," Microsoft said. Windows hotpatches are security updates that don't require a device restart (unless, as in this instance, administrators have to do so to address errors after a hotpatch is installed). Windows 11 hotpatching requires version 24H2 or later, an eligible subscription, and the necessary management and security configuration. "Hotpatch update package size is significantly smaller than the standard cumulative updates," Microsoft said, and the goal is to "streamline the installation process and enhance compliance efficiency." The offending hotpatch, KB5132043 , was released on November 10. It followed the October 13 baseline , which was a prerequisite. Microsoft made hotpatching the default in Windows Autopatch earlier this year. At the time, we asked: " What could possibly go wrong? " Thanks to November's hotpatch, we have our answer. ®

science.title: There's an impostor hiding in the Hyades star cluster. Can you spot it?
science.description: null For years I looked at Taurus and saw something perfectly sensible. There was the Hyades, the big V-shaped cluster that forms the bull's face, with Aldebaran, noticeably brighter and more orange than the other stars, the dominant star. Every diagram reinforced the arrangement — Aldebaran was the eye of Taurus, the Hyades made the face, and in my head they became one object. Then I discovered that Aldebaran has nothing to do with the Hyades. I remember going outside afterward and looking again, half expecting the deception to become obvious now that I knew. It didn't. Aldebaran still looked completely at home among the other stars . The difference is hidden in the one dimension our eyes judge poorly when we look into space — depth. Aldebaran is about 65 light-years away, while the Hyades are roughly 150 light-years distant. The orange eye of Taurus is a foreground star that happens to lie almost exactly along our line of sight toward the Hyades. This fact exposes one of the most convincing tricks in stargazing. The night sky looks flat, and our brains are extremely willing to believe it. But it has incredible depth — and when you can see parts of the night sky in 3D, that's when you begin to appreciate that you're not looking at a flat map. Instead, you begin to see our cosmic neighborhood as it really is. By appreciating depth, you learn its geography. What's happening and when to look Aldebaran, the brightest star in the constellation of Taurus. (Image credit: Christophe Lehenaff via Getty Images) Taurus is now easy to find from the Northern Hemisphere during the evening. Once it's dark, look east for a small, tight knot of stars — the Pleiades open cluster (M45) — and then look nearby for a much larger V-shaped arrangement. That V is the Hyades, with unmistakably orange Aldebaran apparently sitting on one arm. Aldebaran's name is derived from the Arabic Al Dabarān, meaning "the follower," because it appears to trail the Pleiades across the night sky. The Hyades is a real physical group of stars — an open cluster — that formed together and moves through our galaxy together. About 153 light-years away, the Hyades is the nearest open star cluster to Earth. The name means "the rainmakers" because their rising and setting times in the ancient Greek sky coincided with wet weather. The stars in the Hyades are of a similar age — and mostly sun-like stars, or similar — so astronomers can tell that they all formed together in the same nebula . Orange-red star Aldebaran — the 14th-brightest star in the night sky — is the interloper, sitting less than half as far away from the sun . science.description: null The solar system is a clock that can be run in both directions. On Aug. 2, 2027, that clock will bring the moon's dark central shadow — a path of totality — back to Egypt. A t otal solar eclipse will sweep across the country , passing directly over Luxor and plunging some of ancient Egypt's greatest surviving monuments into darkness. Totality will begin in Luxor at approximately 1:02 p.m. EEST and last 6 minutes 22 seconds, according to Time and Date . We know when it will happen because we can calculate the motions of Earth and the moon centuries in advance. But run the same celestial clock backward and eclipses become one of nature's most precise timestamps. Astronomers can reconstruct where the moon's shadow fell thousands of years ago, even when nobody left a record of it. When an ancient text reliably describes an eclipse, it can anchor a moment in history to a specific place and time. Did an eclipse rewrite the Pyramid Age? On April 1, 2471 B.C., a total solar eclipse swept across northern Egypt during the age of the great pyramid builders. In research published in 2025, archaeoastronomer Giulio Magli at the Polytechnic University of Milan proposed that the eclipse may help explain why Pharaoh Shepseskaf broke with tradition and built a huge rectangular tomb at South Saqqara instead of a pyramid. It's a tantalizing hypothesis, but no surviving Egyptian text records the eclipse. Astronomers can calculate that an eclipse happened, but using it as a historical timestamp requires evidence that someone actually saw it and recorded it. science.description: null Last month, the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) released a chilling and info-packed report judging the scope and breadth of threats posed by the nation's adversaries in space. The new report focuses on China , Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea. It looks at what's happening in Earth orbit and beyond, including cislunar space, the region between our planet and the moon . The report — the 2026 edition of "Challenges to Security in Space" — is the third iteration of the DIA's unclassified intelligence assessment on space-related challenges and threats to U.S. national security, as well as the extent to which space is treated internationally as a warfighting domain . Information within the report, which you can read here , is current as of July 2026. DIA's mission is to provide intelligence on foreign militaries to help prevent wars, and win the ones that are fought. Up-front finding The report's up-front finding is that China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea are developing, testing, deploying and using space capabilities "in a way that threatens the security of all space systems and their associated space benefits." Indeed, China and Russia are developing "a formidable spectrum" of offensive capabilities to degrade or destroy space services of other countries, from kinetic destruction to sophisticated jamming and cyber operations. The DIA report also notes that "the production of cheaper, smaller, and simpler satellites , which are faster to develop and deploy, along with the expansion of commercially available launch services, are driving the rapid integration of commercial space alternatives to support national security." While space commercialization is making previously government-centered space services widely available to interested parties, the DIA report adds, that availability also includes state and non-state actors with malign interests. There are a range of threats to space-based services, both commercial and military. Some are reversible, while others are not. (Image credit: DIA) Counterspace worries A major item dealt with by the DIA is "counterspace" — and it's not the kind that you'll find in your kitchen. The Riemann hypothesis was first put forward in 1859 by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann. It proposes an origin for the prime numbers, namely that they follow a certain pattern. The question is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems, which will award a $1 million prize for an accepted solution.
